clue.text: Casual garment from Round 3 in Germany rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the German word just before it is read from its end

blocks.note: a round shape looks like the letter O
3 points to the answer at 3-down, IRON, and the German for iron is Eisen

explanation.surface: A comfy outfit picked up in the third round of some German contest and then turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round 3' reads as a stage of a competition; the 3 is a cross-reference to the answer at 3-down, which then has to be put into German.
explanation.definitionFit: A onesie is a loose all-in-one suit worn for lounging, a casual item of clothing.

clue.text: Former pupil — the only one Lawrence dated

blocks.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil of a school
sole means the only one
T.E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, by his initials

explanation.surface: An old boy recalls being the one pupil a man called Lawrence went out with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dated' sounds like going out with someone; it is the definition, meaning out of date.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obsolete has fallen out of use, just as anything dated belongs to a past era.

clue.text: Rowing crews at 'ouse reel

blocks.note: a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen
at house means at home, and the dropped H of 'ouse is dropped from home too

explanation.surface: Boat crews relaxing at the house strike up a lively Scottish dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'ouse tells you to drop the H from the word you substitute: at home becomes 'ome.
explanation.definitionFit: An eightsome reel is a Scottish country dance for eight people, a kind of reel.

clue.text: Smooth Japanese dish tipped over

indicators.note: in a down clue, something tipped over is turned upside down, so the word runs the other way

blocks.note: nori is the dried seaweed used in Japanese cooking, as in sushi

explanation.surface: A smooth bowl of Japanese food gets knocked off the table.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron clothes is to press them smooth, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Spooner's national hero inclined to provide glamping accommodation

indicators.note: Dr Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words found next have their initial sounds exchanged

blocks.note: William Tell is Switzerland's national hero, and inclined means bent; swapping their first sounds gives the phrase

explanation.surface: A national hero is keen to offer accommodation for well-heeled campers.
explanation.walkthrough: William Tell, the Swiss archer who shot an apple from his son's head, is the national hero here.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell tent is a large round canvas tent, a staple of glamping, or comfortable upmarket camping.

clue.text: Therefore whirling mist causes sickness

indicators.note: something whirling spins around, so the letters of the next word are churned into a new order

blocks.note: ergo is Latin for therefore
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A swirling fog makes people ill, so the argument runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergotism is poisoning caused by eating grain infected with ergot fungus, an illness.

clue.text: Hearkens when Listener is loaned out

blocks.note: first meaning: pays attention to someone
second meaning, read literally: an ear, the organ that listens, being lent to someone

explanation.surface: Someone pays attention when a copy of The Listener magazine is lent out.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital L makes Listener look like the magazine or crossword; it is simply an ear, which in the idiom is lent.
explanation.definitionFit: To lend an ear means to listen attentively, which is what hearkening is.

clue.text: Dainty piece of self-indulgence

indicators.note: a piece of something is only part of it, so the letters sit inside the following words

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the hyphen

explanation.surface: A delicate little treat that is a bit of an indulgence.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means small and delicate like an elf, so it describes something dainty.

clue.text: Having swapped the middle of the red hologram's feature

indicators.note: swapping two central letters changes their order, so the phrase is rearranged in that one spot

blocks.note: taken as written, as one run of letters

explanation.surface: A hologram with the red part switched around shows off its main attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: Run the two words together and exchange the two letters in the middle, the E and the R.
explanation.definitionFit: A hologram gives an image depth, so its defining quality is being three-dimensional.

clue.text: New 'air do and set

indicators.note: a new version of something is made over, so the letters following are put in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written, the H already dropped from hairdo

explanation.surface: A cockney asks for a new hairdo, and has it set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks like part of the hairdressing, but it is the definition, as in a wireless set.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio is a receiving set, and in older usage a set meant a wireless receiver.

clue.text: Leo, say, alternatively a married lady

blocks.note: Leo is an example of a sign of the zodiac
or offers an alternative
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Leo, or else a woman who is married.
explanation.definitionFit: Signora is the Italian title for a married woman, the equivalent of Mrs.

clue.text: Has achieved success after many miles?

definitions.text: Has achieved success after many miles?

blocks.note: the surface reading: someone who has done very well in life
the setter's reading: a literal traveller who has covered a long distance

explanation.surface: Someone has finally made it after a long, hard journey.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for doing well in a career is also a literal description of a long trip.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for success in a career, and taken literally it means having travelled a long distance.

clue.text: A great deal on offer?

blocks.note: first meaning: a large amount
second meaning: items put up for sale at an auction

explanation.surface: Is this a great bargain being sold?
explanation.walkthrough: 'A great deal' suggests a bargain; it is a quantity, and the items on offer are those at an auction.
explanation.definitionFit: Lots means plenty, and lots are also the numbered items offered for bidding in an auction sale.

clue.text: Hints Essex is rebuilt. I have this feeling

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again differently, so these letters are assembled anew

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Clues suggest the county of Essex is being redeveloped, and I sense it coming.
explanation.definitionFit: A sixth sense is an intuition beyond the five senses, a hunch or feeling about what is to come.

clue.text: Literary youngsters such as the Jacksons or Spice Girls

definitions.text: such as the Jacksons or Spice Girls
definitions.note: an example group, singular, standing for any celebrated quintet

blocks.note: first meaning: the child adventurers of Enid Blyton's book series

blocks.clueFragment: such as the Jacksons or Spice Girls
blocks.note: second meaning: a celebrated group of five, like the Jackson 5 or the five Spice Girls

explanation.surface: Young characters from books are compared to famous family and girl pop groups.
explanation.walkthrough: Enid Blyton's children's books follow four children and a dog; the Jackson 5 and the Spice Girls were both well-known five-member pop acts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Famous Five are Blyton's young heroes, and any well-known quintet of performers could be called a famous five.

clue.text: Involving shared responsibility with traffic in both directions

blocks.note: first meaning: a mutual arrangement where both sides contribute
second meaning: describing a street where vehicles run both ways

explanation.walkthrough: One adjective covers both a mutual relationship and a road open to vehicles going either way.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated adjective describes reciprocal arrangements and also streets that allow travel in either direction.

clue.text: Stupid, like one number

blocks.note: as means like, in a comparison
I is the Roman numeral for one
nine is a number

explanation.surface: It is foolish to think of yourself as just a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means as silly as an ass, which is to say foolish or stupid.

clue.text: Love attention, being comparatively mischievous

blocks.note: love is nought, a zero score in tennis, and attention is an ear, as in giving someone your ear

explanation.surface: Craving the spotlight makes a child behave worse.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no word to signal sound here: the two words for love and attention, said together, run into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Naughtier is the comparative form of naughty, so it means more mischievous than another.

clue.text: e.g. mostly butter spread around a crusty stick

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word that follows is dropped
something spread is smeared out of shape, so the letters are put in a new arrangement
around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters enclose the single letter after it

blocks.note: taken as written
the word without its final letter
taken as written, placed inside

explanation.surface: Butter, for instance, is smeared over most of a crunchy loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A baguette is a long thin French loaf with a hard crust, so it is a crusty stick of bread.

clue.text: Two sets of miners on review for boardgame

indicators.note: a review looks things over again and re-sorts them, so these letters are put back in another order

blocks.note: the word miners written out twice
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two shifts of colliers are inspected for a game played on a board.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine men's morris is an ancient strategy game where each player moves nine pieces on a board of lines.

clue.text: No time for hackers' cyber-attack on software

blocks.note: zero means none at all
a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: Computer users have no time to deal with an online assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A zero-day attack exploits a software flaw before the developer knows of it, leaving zero days to fix it.

clue.text: Silky hound called Sarah — our country's number one

blocks.note: Sal is a pet form of the name Sarah
the setter's own country, the United Kingdom
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sleek dog named Sarah is the best in the land.
explanation.definitionFit: The saluki is a slender Middle Eastern sighthound with a smooth, silky coat.

clue.text: Don't begin undressing in the near future

definitions.note: the answer is a noun used in the phrase 'in the offing'

indicators.note: not beginning means losing the opening letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: doffing means taking off clothes; it loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone advises against starting to strip any time soon.
explanation.definitionFit: The offing is the stretch of sea visible offshore, and 'in the offing' means coming soon.

clue.text: Said 'Super' which does jar!

indicators.note: said means spoken out loud, so the answer sounds like the word for the next idea

blocks.note: super means great, a word pronounced identically to a word with a different spelling

explanation.surface: Someone exclaimed 'Super' in a way that was irritating.
explanation.definitionFit: To grate on someone is to jar or irritate, as a harsh sound jars on the ear.

clue.text: 16 standing firm

blocks.note: first meaning: sixteen is ..., four times four
second meaning: resolute and unwavering

explanation.walkthrough: The 16 looks like a cross-reference to 16-across, as numbers do in this puzzle, but here it is the plain number.
explanation.definitionFit: Foursquare means solidly based and firmly resolute, and the two words also describe sixteen as the square of four.

clue.text: Army group hugging female out of shape

indicators.note: hugging means wrapping your arms around, so the army word encloses the letter for female

blocks.note: a unit is a military formation
F is the standard abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A soldier's group embraces a woman who is not in good condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfit means not in good physical condition, which is to say out of shape.

clue.text: Hose — otherwise, what else could be worn!

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters are arranged differently

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: If not stockings, what other item would anyone wear on their feet?
explanation.walkthrough: Hose are stockings, and the exclamation points to another item worn on the feet alongside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe is footwear, the obvious other thing to wear on the feet with hose.

clue.text: Menu option some found odd

indicators.note: some means a portion, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A choice on the restaurant menu that a few diners thought strange.
explanation.walkthrough: The menu is the computer kind, not a restaurant's.
explanation.definitionFit: Undo is a standard command in software menus that reverses the last action.

clue.text: Deal out punishment to popular cop before start of trial

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
flic is French slang for a police officer
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A well-liked police officer is penalised just as the court case opens.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflict is to impose something unpleasant such as a penalty, dealing it out to someone.

clue.text: Working in steel that can be stretched

indicators.note: metal that is being worked is beaten into a new shape, so these letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A metalworker shapes steel that has some give in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tensile describes a material able to be drawn out or stretched under tension.

clue.text: Is revenged with Georgia re-arranging events

indicators.note: re-arranging means putting things in another order, so the letters of the next word move about

blocks.note: GE is the international country code for Georgia
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone takes revenge by reorganising events in Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: Georgia usually gives GA for the US state; here it is the country, coded GE.
explanation.definitionFit: To get even is to pay someone back for a wrong, which is to take revenge.
